security_audit.summary: Most static backtick findings are Markdown formatting or documentation examples, but the installer command at SKILL.md:17 is a confirmed critical pipe-to-shell risk. Several infsh and npx examples are real external command guidance, and the skill intentionally sends TSX code and props to inference.sh. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed file.

remediation.suggestion: Remove curl-to-sh installation. Provide a pinned release download, checksum verification steps, and a separate infsh login command.
Warn users before sending TSX, props, media URLs, or credentials to inference.sh. Document data retention and privacy expectations.
Replace npx skills add examples with links, or require explicit user confirmation before installing additional skills.

content.user_title: Render Remotion Videos from React Code
content.value_statement: Teams need repeatable video rendering without managing a local Remotion pipeline. This skill sends React/Remotion components to inference.sh and returns an MP4.
actual_capabilities: Runs inference.sh Remotion render jobs from TSX component input.
Accepts duration, frame rate, size, codec, composition ID, and props.
Uses Remotion primitives such as AbsoluteFill, Sequence, spring, and interpolate.
Supports CLI examples and Python SDK usage for rendering workflows.
Streams render progress when the Python SDK uses streaming.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh CLI or SDK and an authenticated account.
Uploads component code and props to an external inference.sh service.
Does not provide local Remotion project scaffolding or asset management.
Render success depends on supported imports and valid TSX component code.

use_cases.title: Create Branded Motion Graphics
use_cases.description: Render repeatable title cards, product clips, and social videos from reusable React components.

use_cases.title: Automate Video Generation
use_cases.description: Turn application data and props into consistent MP4 videos without maintaining a local render farm.

use_cases.title: Render Data-Driven Updates
use_cases.description: Produce animated counters, charts, and status clips from structured inputs and controlled timing.

prompt_templates.title: Render a Simple Intro

prompt_templates.prompt: Use remotion-render to create a three-second intro video with my title, dark background, and smooth fade-in.

prompt_templates.title: Animate a Counter
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request using props and frame timing.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a square Remotion counter video from 0 to 100 percent, then render it at 1080 by 1080 and 60 fps.

prompt_templates.title: Build Timed Scenes
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a multi-section sequence.
prompt_templates.prompt: Render a product update video with three timed scenes, staggered text, spring motion, and a final call-to-action.

prompt_templates.title: Stream Render Progress
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow using the Python SDK.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Python SDK workflow to submit a longer Remotion render and report progress until the MP4 is available.

best_practices: Review TSX code and props before sending them to inference.sh.
Use explicit width, height, fps, and duration for predictable output.
Keep media URLs stable and accessible for the full render duration.
anti_patterns: Do not include secrets, private source, or credentials in render props.
Do not run installer commands without reviewing the download and checksum process.
Do not rely on unsupported imports or browser-only APIs inside the component.

faq.question: What does this skill render?
faq.answer: It renders React/Remotion TSX components into MP4 videos through inference.sh.

faq.question: Does it require an inference.sh account?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples use the inference.sh CLI or SDK and require authentication.

faq.question: Can I pass custom props?
faq.answer: Yes. The input schema includes a props object that is passed to the exported component.

faq.question: Can it render local files automatically?
faq.answer: No. Assets must be available to the render environment, usually through accessible URLs or supported inputs.

faq.question: Is my code sent to a third party?
faq.answer: Yes. The component code and props are submitted to inference.sh for rendering.

faq.question: What security review is needed before use?
faq.answer: Review installer commands, avoid sensitive inputs, and confirm that external rendering is acceptable for your project.
